title: How to Add a launch screen in Xcode in Xcode on Mac for developers
metaTitle: How to Add a launch screen in Xcode on Mac: Step by Step
description: Learn how to add a launch screen in Xcode on Mac. Follow our guide to configure your launch screen storyboard or Info.plist settings for your iOS projects.
targetKeyword: how to add a launch screen in xcode on mac
intro: To add a launch screen in Xcode on Mac, you can either create a dedicated launch screen storyboard file or configure the Info.plist settings directly. These methods ensure your app displays a system-managed interface immediately upon startup to improve the perceived performance.
tldr: Use the Storyboard method for complex, multi-element launch layouts.
Use the Info.plist method for simple, static color or image backgrounds.
Clean your build folder if changes do not appear on the simulator.
Keep individual images under 0.5 MB to avoid potential rendering issues.

blocks.text: Why Your App Needs a Launch Screen

A launch screen is the first thing a user sees when they open your app. It is not a splash screen meant for branding or animations. Instead, it acts as a placeholder while the system initializes your app. A well-designed launch screen creates a smooth transition from the home screen to your app's first view controller. If the transition is jarring, users may perceive your app as sluggish or unpolished. Apple requires this for iOS, iPadOS, and tvOS apps to ensure a consistent experience.
Method 1: Using a Launch Screen Storyboard

The storyboard method is the most flexible way to manage your launch interface. It allows you to use Auto Layout to ensure your content centers perfectly across different screen sizes and device orientations. This is the recommended approach for most modern iOS applications.

items: Press ⌘ N to open the new file menu.
Select iOS at the top, then choose Launch Screen under the User Interface section.
Name your file, typically LaunchScreen.storyboard, and click Create.
Open the new file and drag UI elements like labels or images onto the canvas.
Apply Auto Layout constraints to pin your elements to the Superview.
In the Attributes Inspector, ensure the Is Initial View Controller checkbox is selected.

blocks.text: For apps that only require a simple background color or a single static logo, you can avoid storyboards entirely. Defining these settings in the Info.plist is straightforward and keeps your project file count lower. This is ideal for minimal app designs.

items: Select your project in the Project navigator.
Navigate to the Info tab in your target settings.
Hover over any key in the Custom iOS Target Properties section and click the (+) button.
Add the UILaunchScreen key and press Return.
Expand the dictionary and add sub-keys such as UIImageName or UIColorName.
Provide the names of your assets from your asset catalog.

blocks.text: Developers often face issues where the launch screen appears black or does not update after changes. This is usually due to aggressive system caching. To force an update, delete the app from your simulator or physical device, then clean your build folder by pressing ⇧ ⌘ K. Always verify that your images are under 0.5 MB to prevent rendering errors. Using images larger than 25 MB will cause the system to ignore your launch screen entirely.

faq.question: Do I need a launch screen for macOS apps?
faq.answer: No. Launch screens are specifically required for iOS, iPadOS, and tvOS. macOS applications handle their initial window differently.

faq.question: Why is my launch screen showing as a black screen?
faq.answer: This is often caused by image files that are too large. Ensure your assets are under 0.5 MB for optimal performance and stability.

faq.question: How do I force the simulator to show my new launch screen?
faq.answer: Delete the app from the simulator, clean your build folder with ⇧ ⌘ K, and perform a fresh build and run.

task: Add a launch screen in Xcode
requirements: Basic knowledge of the Project Navigator

steps.name: Open Project Settings
steps.text: Click the project icon in the top of the Navigator sidebar to open your project settings.

steps.name: Select Launch Screen File
steps.text: Navigate to the General tab and locate the App Icons and Launch Screen section to select your file.

steps.name: Clean Build Folder
steps.text: If changes do not appear, clean your build folder to remove cached data.

troubleshooting.problem: Launch screen not updating in simulator
troubleshooting.fix: Delete the app from the simulator and clean the build folder.
Check that your image assets are under 0.5 MB.

lazur.spoken: Where do I set the launch screen file?
lazur.result: Lazur circles the Launch Screen File dropdown in your project settings.
